root_cause.text: The iomap read path fails to hand off folio ownership to the IO helper when the IO granularity is smaller than the folio size and no per-folio state (ifs) is attached, allowing iomap_read_end() to be called on a folio already owned by the IO helper, leading to use-after-free or double completion.
root_cause.evidence: The patch modifies the condition `if (*bytes_submitted == folio_len)` to also include `|| !ifs`, so that when there is no iomap_folio_state (i.e., the !ifs case), ctx->cur_folio is unconditionally set to NULL. The CVE description explains that the previous check failed to invalidate the folio when ``1 << i_blkbits`` matches the folio size but the IO granularity is smaller, causing partial folio submissions without proper ownership transfer.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function shows that `read_count` is only incremented when `iop` is non-NULL (lines 290-291: `if (!same_page && iop) atomic_inc(&iop->read_count);` and lines 300-301: `if (iop) atomic_inc(&iop->read_count);`). When `iop` is NULL (e.g., memory allocation failure in `iomap_page_create` at line 256), no read counting is performed. If the IO granularity is smaller than the page size (i.e., `plen < PAGE_SIZE` from `iomap_adjust_read_range` at line 269), multiple bios may be needed to cover the full page. However, without a `read_count` mechanism, the completion handler (`iomap_read_end_io`) will treat the page as fully done after the first bio completes, leading to a use-after-free or double completion when subsequent bios complete. The commit only adds fallback bio allocation on failure (lines 319-320) but does not fix the missing ownership handoff for the no-iop case, so the vulnerable construct remains and is not fixed.
